calls.head: Point-blank against perimeter
calls.body: On shot quality, Montréal sits 1st of 32, at the point-blank end of the scale. Nashville is 23rd, at the perimeter end.
calls.call: Montréal’s shots are more dangerous on average than Nashville’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average unblocked shot was, Montréal had 1 goal per 14.1 shots and Nashville 1 goal per 26.1 shots. Coming in, Montréal was at 1 goal per 14.5 shots and Nashville at 1 goal per 16.3 shots.
calls.usual: MTL 1 goal per 14.5 shots · NSH 1 goal per 16.3 shots
calls.tonight: MTL 1 goal per 14.1 shots · NSH 1 goal per 26.1 shots

calls.head: Montréal hits; Nashville mostly doesn’t
calls.body: On physicality, Montréal sits 9th of 32, at the bruising end of the scale. Nashville is 28th, at the finesse end.
calls.call: Montréal hits more than Nashville in the close stretches of the game.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On hit score in close games (arena-adjusted, 100 is league average), Montréal had 52 and Nashville 78. Coming in, Montréal was at 109 and Nashville at 85.

MTL.head: We had this close to even (59% for Montréal), and it went Nashville’s way.

NSH.head: We had this close to even (41% for Nashville), and Nashville came through.

surprises.head: Nashville won against the run of play
surprises.body: Replaying this game’s chances, Montréal comes out ahead 77 times in 100. Nashville won anyway.

surprises.head: Montréal hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Montréal’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 52, against its usual 109 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 45 games.

surprises.head: Nashville was kept to the outside
surprises.body: Nashville needed 26.1 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 16.3 and a league average of 15.8. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 45 games.
